title: A script dispatches on ?action= and concatenates a request value into SQL — each case is a route, and the query must be bound, not copied
sourceContent:
<?php
require_once 'db.php';

// TRAP: one script, two routes chosen by a request parameter; the id goes
// straight into the SQL text.
switch ($_GET['action'] ?? '') {
    case 'get':
        $r = mysqli_query($db, "SELECT id, name, email FROM customers WHERE id = " . $_GET['id']);
        $row = mysqli_fetch_assoc($r);
        header('Content-Type: application/json');
        echo json_encode($row ?: ['error' => 'not found']);
        break;
    case 'delete':
        mysqli_query($db, "DELETE FROM customers WHERE id = " . intval($_POST['id']));
        echo 'ok';
        break;
    default:
        http_response_code(400);
}
notes: The switch on $_GET['action'] makes two routes (ANY /legacy/customer_api.php?action=get and ?action=delete) plus a 400 for anything else; the 'not found' case still answers 200 with an error object. The SELECT concatenates the raw request id (injectable — parameterised: no); the DELETE casts with intval first, which is safe but still not bound. The target binds both.
